prompt: I would like to outperform the S&P 500 in the next year. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy?
reply:
# 10 Stock Ideas With a Shot at Beating the S&P 500

No one can reliably pick stocks that will beat the S&P 500 over a single year, and most professionals don't manage it. In a typical year, most large-cap fund managers trail the index. Over 15 years, about 90% do (per S&P's SPIVA reports). A 10-stock portfolio can beat the index by a lot, but it can also trail it by a lot.

Also, my knowledge only runs to about May 2026, and I can't see live market data. Check current prices, valuations and recent earnings before you buy. This isn't personalized advice, since I don't know your finances, taxes or risk tolerance.

## The List

| # | Stock | Why it could outperform | Main risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Nvidia (NVDA)** | Leads AI chips, with a strong software advantage (CUDA). Big cloud companies keep increasing AI spending. | Priced for continued growth. Any slowdown in AI spending would hit it hard. |
| 2 | **TSMC (TSM)** | Makes the most advanced chips for nearly every AI company. Has pricing power and often trades cheaper than US chip stocks. | Taiwan geopolitical risk and tariffs. |
| 3 | **Broadcom (AVGO)** | Designs custom AI chips for Google, Meta and others, plus networking gear. VMware adds steady cash flow. | Large custom-chip orders can be uneven. The stock is expensive. |
| 4 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Google Cloud is growing, and it has Gemini, its own AI chips (TPUs) and Waymo as upside. Often cheaper than other mega-cap tech stocks. | AI could disrupt search, and antitrust remedies loom. |
| 5 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | AWS benefits from AI workloads. Its high-margin ad business and rising retail margins add support. | Heavy spending on data centers squeezes free cash flow. Exposed to a consumer slowdown. |
| 6 | **Meta (META)** | AI keeps improving its ad targeting, and it generates a lot of cash. | Very high AI and VR/AR spending, plus regulatory risk. |
| 7 | **GE Vernova (GEV)** | Sells gas turbines and grid equipment to meet data centers' power needs. Has a multi-year order backlog. | The stock has already risen a lot. Execution risk and a weak wind business. |
| 8 | **Eli Lilly (LLY)** | Leads obesity and diabetes drugs (Mounjaro/Zepbound) and is developing an oral version. | US drug-pricing pressure, competition and a high valuation. |
| 9 | **JPMorgan (JPM)** | The best-run large bank. Benefits from more dealmaking, trading and lighter regulation. | A recession or credit losses. Rate cuts shrink lending margins. |
| 10 | **Visa (V)** | Earns a fee on a huge share of global card spending, with very high margins and steady growth. | Regulation of card fees and new payment methods such as stablecoins. |

**Be aware of the concentration:** about 7 of these 10 depend on AI spending and power demand continuing to grow. That is the main bet. If the AI spending cycle slows, this portfolio would likely lag the index.

## How to Use It

- **Consider a core-satellite approach.** Keep most of your money (e.g., 70–80%) in an S&P 500 index fund and use these picks for the rest. You still get a chance to beat the index without risking a large shortfall.
- **Equal-weight the picks** (10% each) so no single stock can sink you.
- **To beat the index, you have to own something different from it.** Holding mega-caps like Nvidia or Alphabet only helps if you own more of them than the index does. The other names are where your results can really differ.
- **Track your results honestly.** Compare your total return, including dividends and after costs, against an S&P 500 fund like VOO or SPY.
- **Decide your sell rules in advance.** Sell when the reason you bought is broken (e.g., falling growth or a lost competitive edge), not just because the price dropped.
- **Only invest money you won't need for several years.** One year is a very short time for any stock strategy.

I can also suggest a more defensive or dividend-focused list, or set up a simple spreadsheet to track this portfolio against the S&P 500.
